changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 5 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6357-basechema-bind-declaration.md`

- names `content/docs/fields/grid.mdx` → `content/docs/fields/grid.mdx` — edited by this change

  > `bind` was read by ten production sites and declared by no schema shape. It resolved as `any` through `BaseSchema`'s index signature and rode `.passthrough()` on the validator, while three separate documents taught it as an authorable key of *every* node: this repo's own `AGENTS.md` §4 ("Every node in the UI tree follows this shape (`@object-ui/types`)"), the published agent-facing `skills/objectui/rules/protocol.md` ("Every UI component node MUST follow this shape"), and `content/docs/fields/grid.mdx`. So the agent-facing protocol told authors to write a key the published types did not know existed.

### `.changeset/6625-retire-fieldmeta-decimals.md`

- names `fields/src/index.tsx` → `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `buildFieldMeta` computed `decimals: overrides.decimals ?? meta?.decimals ?? meta?.scale` on **every** call and the value **reached nothing**. Re-measured on this branch's base (`efdc6c62`): **zero `.decimals` member reads** across `@object-ui/fields`, `@object-ui/i18n`, `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/core` and `plugin-dashboard` itself — the only non-comment occurrence was the write being removed here. The **positive control in the same query shape** fires: `.scale` member reads hit `NumberField.tsx`, `GridField.tsx` and `fields/src/index.tsx`. So the zero is a finding, not a broken query. The `overrides.decimals ??` head of that chain had already lost its only feeder when objectui#6425's ruling removed the authored read from `ObjectDataTable.enrich()`; `RecordDetailDrawer`, the only other `buildFieldMeta` caller, passes no overrides at all. Both halves retire together, so the key leaves in one move.

### `.changeset/6694-dashboard-lookup-reference-meta.md`

- names `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` → `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` — edited by this change

  > ⚠️ The copy set is three keys where `ObjectGrid`'s `RELATIONAL_META_KEYS` is nine, and the difference is measured per key, not preferred. The grid's cells are EDITABLE, so its extra keys drive the inline picker's query (`LookupField` / `UserField` read `id_field`, `description_field`, `lookup_filters`, `lookupFilters`); these two widgets are read-only and their render path ends at a cell renderer. `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` reads exactly `reference_to`, `reference` and `display_field` off a cell's `field` prop; `titleFormat` is never read off a field meta at all (its readers take it off the object schema, which arrives here through `useRefObjectSchema(reference_to)`), and `reference_to_field` has zero member reads anywhere in the repo. Copying the other six would mint six members written on every call and read by nothing — precisely what objectui#6625 (`decimals`) and objectui#6597 (`referenceTo`) retired from this same file.

### `.changeset/6837-reference-to-arm-deletion.md`

- names `fields/src/index.tsx` → `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Three readers were deliberately left alone.** `LookupCellRenderer` (`fields/src/index.tsx`), `LookupField` and `UserField` read `FieldMetadata` — ObjectUI's OWN contract, whose `LookupFieldMetadata` declares `reference_to` and never declares `reference`. They are fed by the emitters above and by published example schemas (`examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/fields-lookup/*.json`), so narrowing them would break in-repo producers, and `plugin-grid`'s `relationalMetaCopySet.derivation.test.ts` re-derives its read set from exactly those three sources — where `reference_to` is recorded with verdict `adapter-stamped`. `DetailViewFieldSchema` is likewise untouched.

### `.changeset/7166-retire-inert-fieldmeta-copies.md`

- names `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` → `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `applyRelationalMeta` writes the copy set onto the `fieldMeta` that `generateColumns` hands to `ANGLE-BRACKETS(CellRenderer)` as the `field` prop — six JSX passes across the three column-building paths, and nowhere else. For a relational column that resolves to `LookupCellRenderer`, which reads exactly `reference_to`, `reference`, `display_field`, `displayField`, `reference_field` and `options`; a `user` column resolves to `UserCellRenderer`, which destructures `{ value }` and reads no field meta at all. Measured by receiver rather than by count: `packages/fields/src/index.tsx`, the file holding **every** cell renderer, contains **zero** occurrences of the three retired keys, against a control of 22 occurrences of the `display_field` / `displayField` / `reference_to` spellings the cell does read.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Angle-bracketed names in the quoted prose above are rewritten as `ANGLE-BRACKETS(name)`: GitHub deletes tag-shaped fragments from a stored body, and a quote that silently loses the identifier it is about is worse than a visible repair.

Compared the checked-out tree with `09ab32bff` (merge-base with origin/main): 8 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1424 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2006 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36104137228)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0cf9eaf456a199945c6749912e5efdccd4b38663`

### ① Derived judgments

Read against the card body, the cross-link comment 5592405775, the triage 5619307943 (the binding text: "Masking a populated `password` is correct and must stay. Drawing the mask over `null` is the defect. ⇒ the deliverable is that the **empty** cases become distinguishable from populated ones, ⛔ not that the four start printing their values. Any change that reveals secret content is out of scope"), the objectui#8440 ruling A, the objectui#8596 string-class ruling, and `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` (the lockfile's resolution; read from the published tarball into scratch because the shared checkout carries no `node_modules`). Every line cited is at head 0cf9eaf. Merge-base with main is bc4efba732a31acd206066104a3210d1ec9379ed.

Behaviour changes, one by one:

1. `packages/fields/src/index.tsx:3377-3378` — `password` and `secret` now point at the named, unexported `MaskedCellRenderer` (`index.tsx:3274-3277`). Predicate `isEmptyValue(coerceToSafeValue(value))`, which is byte-for-byte `TextCellRenderer`'s own test (`index.tsx:728-736`). Empty ⇒ the shared `EmptyValue` (a span with `data-slot` empty-value and aria-label "No value", `packages/components/src/custom/empty.tsx:155-174`); otherwise the same six-bullet span as at the base. RIGHT: matches the triage deliverable exactly; the value is never read beyond presence, so nothing is revealed. `{}` coerces to `[Object]` and keeps the mask (`coerceToSafeValue.ts:79`), which is the objectui#8596 string-class answer ("the record IS storing something") applied to two `STRING_VALUE_TYPES` members (spec `src/data/field-value.zod.ts:56-60` lists `password` and `secret`). A whitespace-only string keeps the mask because `text` keeps its spaces. `['']` joins to `''` and draws the affordance, as `text` does. Consistent per class.
2. `index.tsx:3388-3389` — `vector` and `grid` now point at `VectorCellRenderer` / `GridCellRenderer` (`index.tsx:3304-3312`), predicate the floor exactly (`isEmptyValue`, `packages/core/src/utils/emptiness.ts:97-104`: `null`, `undefined`, `''`, `[]`). RIGHT: the triage names a constant face over nothing as the defect; the cross-link comment says these two have no masking rationale. `[]` is a genuine empty member of `vector`'s class (spec `valueSchemaFor` returns `z.array(z.number())`, `field-value.zod.ts:538`) and of `GridField`'s array-of-rows contract (`GridField.tsx:712` writes arrays). `{}` deliberately NOT swept: `hasCellValue` (`plugin-detail/src/emptiness.ts:150-156`) calls every populated object a value, so a `{}` clause would put "No value" inside a row that band calls filled; and the spec write seam refuses a non-array vector (pinned as PREMISE). Reasoned from the contract, not from the card; RIGHT.
3. The populated face for all four is byte-identical to the base (the same two span spellings). RIGHT: "must stay", and pinned as bytes (POPULATED in the new file).
4. `index.tsx:365-373` roster docblock and `index.tsx:3313-3328` table docblock rewritten. Both true at head: the three renderers ask the floor by name, and I read the whole table `index.tsx:3329-3392` and found no arrow entry left. The table is still a function; the docblock now says the difference is no longer observable through identity, which is accurate.
5. The three consumers that quote the mask were checked: `ObjectGrid` column cells pass the raw value straight to the renderer (`plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx:3409`), so the change reaches a grid column as the changeset says; `DetailSection` and `HeaderHighlight` pre-guard with `hasCellValue`, so they never drew the mask over `null` and are unchanged; gallery omits floor-empty rows before resolving (`ObjectGallery.tsx:635`).

Asked and missing: nothing. The triage asked the dev to make the scope judgement explicitly (done in the PR body's per-class table and in the docblocks), to read objectui#8440 first (done; the copy gate reads `hasCellValue` plus the plugin-detail mirror set and is untouched), and the card asked for a check against the existing pins and for consumers depending on the mask always rendering (the four test files in `packages/fields` that name the faces were all adjusted or re-read; the two in `plugin-detail` measure a populated object value and still hold).

Done but not asked: the three docs pages (`content/docs/fields/grid.mdx:181-182`, `vector.mdx:88-89`, `password.mdx:50-55`) — required by AGENTS.md #2, and each pre-existing "renders: [Vector]" / "[Grid]" example line is still true for a stored value. The new IDENTITY pin covers every registered type rather than the four; extra but harmless. The claim's file surface was exceeded (declared under Acceptance notes) by docblocks in the same file, three existing pins, and the docs pages; each is forced by the change, none overlaps an open PR per the body, and the record here treats that as a disclosed deviation, not a defect.

Existing pins edited:

- `cellRenderers.signatureValueClass-8677.test.tsx:118-127, 202-217` — the old THE CENSUS required `password` / `secret` to draw the same bytes for `null` as for a value, i.e. it pinned this card's defect. Flip is load-bearing. The replacement is stronger, not weaker: one face for `alpha`, `bravo` and `{}` (so a member that starts printing its value still fails), the stored value asserted absent from the DOM, no affordance for a value, and the affordance for `null`. The `VALUE_INDEPENDENT_FACES` to `MASKED_FACES` rename keeps the "an exclusion must name a class member" control.
- `cellRenderers.countLabelI18n-8441.test.tsx:351-371` — the retired control asserted `getCellRenderer('vector')` differs across two calls. It could only be true while `vector` was an arrow entry, and there is no arrow entry left, so the control has no subject. The property the 8441 describe guards (a hook-holding entry is one component type across renders) is now pinned table-wide by IDENTITY in the new file, and my Leg A shows it goes red by name. Not a weakened guard; the repeater `toBe` pin itself is untouched.
- `cellRenderers.objectLiteral-8596.test.tsx:281-288` — comment label only; the four `{}` rows and their expected bytes are unchanged, and the file's THE BOUNDARY loops do not include the four types, so nothing in it was asserting the old `null` face.

New pin `cellRenderers.valueIndependent-8678.test.tsx` (37 tests). Lit controls: POPULATED (lines 216-237) pins the exact pre-change bytes and the DOM absence of `sk_live_do_not_render`; THE RULE control (207-213) proves `text` separates `null` from `{}` so the byte-equality is not against a constant; PREMISE (141-149) proves the vector schema accepts a real embedding before asserting the `{}` refusal; IDENTITY asserts a non-empty registry first. Negative legs, run by me in a scratch export of the head (never the shared checkout) with `pnpm install --offline` from the lockfile, four files, positive run 109 passed / 0 failed with the index blob equal to the head blob 0b5e83a8bbfd5f69e2914821fe0efc06511b927c; every mutation anchor hit exactly once and each restore was proven by blob equality:
  - Leg A (four entries back to the base arrows): 20 red — 16 CENSUS empty rows, 2 RULE, IDENTITY naming the four, and 8677's THE CENSUS. 8441 and 8596 stay green, as expected (they did not assert the empty face).
  - Leg C (caricature: masked renderer draws the affordance for everything): 13 red — 2 CENSUS `{}` rows, 2 RULE, 4 POPULATED, 2 BOUNDARY, plus 8596's census and POPULATED and 8677's THE CENSUS.
  - Leg B (vector draws the affordance for everything): 5 red — the vector `{}`, POPULATED and BOUNDARY rows plus 8596's two.
  All three legs redden in the expected direction and the failure sets are the families each leg mutates.

### ② Semver level
